searchText: Has anyone calculated what the approximate opportunity cost per gas for transaction inclusion is in ETH2? A long time ago <@273808422753796097> wrote up a blog post discussing how one can estimate the opportunity cost for inclusion, but it was based on ETH miner block reward. Can the same algorithm be used for ETH2 or is the situation sufficiently different? How does this change with sharding? <jadler> There's no increased orphan risk with larger blocks, so I imagine it's close to zero up until the block gas limit (which should tweaked such that everyone has time under normal network conditions to vote on the block, i.e. such that up until that limit the opportunity cost of gas is ~0). Hmm, interesting. Orphan risk is really 0 or epsilon regardless of block size? Reading in the notes about the workshop, how public will that be? If we have someone who takes notes I think they will be public. There is nothing secret about the workshop, but it is quite focused, and we can only have so many people ask questions before workshop time runs out. The workshop will certainly be recorded and shared. The primary angle here is education Thanks, that's what I meant by public I don't agree that there's no increased risk of large blocks being orphaned. We're seeing a lot of blocks in the first slot of the epoch be orphaned because their processing time is higher (there's a spec change coming to fix that, plus client optimisations done & in progress). When you add in transaction execution, more full blocks will similarly take more time to create and more time to propagate around the network, increasing the risk of being orphaned. I'm not even sure the risk is lower, in PoW on average you have 14 seconds or so before the next one is found, in Eth2 you only have 4 seconds until attestations are generated.
